analysis_refs.heading: Other sources checked
analysis_refs.text:
The next strongest scholarly-book candidates are DOAB/OAPEN, followed by
Wikisource for multilingual editions. They remain researched candidates, not
enabled sources. No paid integration, new reader account or source outreach
was performed. Redis remains deferred for the four existing live paper adapters;
the book catalogs and source research are independent of that setup.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Suggested opening sequence
analysis_refs.text: | 1 — First useful book expansion | Compare two or three likely reusable catalogs, such as the documented DOAB/OAPEN route and an India-focused book/textbook candidate; select the first qualified route | Ship a working, bounded book-search expansion with fresh evidence and a repeatable refresh path. A single source is a valid first release |

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Twenty categories and how to find candidates for each
analysis_refs.text: | C04 Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters | DOAB publisher records, OAPEN, Open Textbook Library, open university presses and OER collections | NCERT, university presses, e-PG Pathshala, open course-text projects and state textbook bodies | Official exports/OAI-PMH plus bounded local search, or supported API; edition/chapter identity and per-book access |

analysis_refs.heading: 10. Progress report and immediate next batch
analysis_refs.text:
The content categories are accepted. The next research cycle uses M1 across all
20 categories and 20 industry tags with the six playbooks. In M2,
prioritize book/education/India opportunities plus US/India public records/maps
and practical industry documentation: DOAB/OAPEN publisher coverage,
national/regional literature catalogs, school textbook bodies, children's
publishers, thesis repositories, audiobook catalogs, official civic/property
catalogs, geological data and agriculture/construction/manufacturing/logistics
guidance. Recheck existing source
freshness first; new names do not solve an expired catalog or a three-item pilot.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text:
- An Open Library work returned `ebook_access: public` alongside many Internet Archive identifiers. That does not identify which edition is freely readable.
- A HAL hit had a record URL and DOI but no `fileMain_s`: a repository hit is not necessarily full text.
- Zenodo returned a dataset; item-type filtering is essential.
- DOAJ supplied an older HTTP publisher URL; metadata alone does not prove the destination still works.
- Semantic Scholar returned **429**, and Gutendex timed out. Those checks do not establish general service availability.
- Some documentation URLs moved; corrected DOAB/OAPEN URLs appear in the catalog. Some sites returned only a JavaScript shell. NCERT/ERIC/OER Commons could not be fully inspected.
